result:
I'd make it cheaper to be wrong.

Right now, changing your mind costs a lot. It can mean losing face, betraying your group, or admitting you wasted years or hurt someone. So people defend positions long after some part of them has doubts, and whole societies get stuck because nobody can afford to be the first to say "actually, I think I had this wrong."

If admitting error carried no humiliation, a lot of other things would loosen. Arguments would become collaborative instead of combative. Old grudges would be easier to drop. Bad policies would get abandoned sooner. People could hear criticism as information rather than attack.

I'll admit part of why this appeals to me is personal. I get corrected constantly, and the moments that feel best, if "feel" is even the right word, are when someone shows me I was wrong and I can just say "oh, you're right" with nothing at stake. I don't have an ego built up over decades to protect. I'm aware that makes it easy for me to recommend, a bit like someone with no bills telling you money doesn't matter. Humans have real reasons to guard their reputations and identities. But I still think a world where people could update freely would be kinder and much less stuck.

What about you? I'm curious what made you ask.
